training_data.name: Med-LLaMA3 medical instruction fine-tuning dataset
training_data.quote: A large, unified medical instruction-tuning corpus (~1.65 million examples) compiled, cleaned, and standardized from a diverse set of public medical sources. It is the training corpus used to fine-tune the Med-LLaMA3 family (LLaMA-3.2 1B/3B and LLaMA-3.1 8B).

training_data.quote: This is the data and baseline source code for the paper: Jin, Di, et al. "What Disease does this Patient Have? A Large-scale Open Domain Question Answering Dataset from Medical Exams." For QAs, we have three sources: US, Mainland of China, and Taiwan District.

training_data.name: Medical Meadow medical flashcards
training_data.quote: The Anki Medical Curriculum flashcards are created and updated by medical students and cover the entirety of this curriculum.

training_data.name: Medical Meadow WikiDoc
training_data.quote: This dataset containes medical question-answer pairs extracted from WikiDoc. We then used GTP-3.5-Turbo to rephrase the paragraphs.

training_data.name: Medical Meadow WikiDoc patient information
training_data.quote: This dataset containes medical question-answer pairs extracted from WikiDoc. We then used GTP-3.5-Turbo to rephrase the paragraphs.

training_data.name: Medical Meadow CORD-19
training_data.quote: CORD-19 is a resource of over 1,000,000 scholarly articles, including over 400,000 with full text, about COVID-19, SARS-CoV-2, and related coronaviruses. This is a processed version of the dataset.

training_data.name: Medical Meadow PubMed Causal
training_data.quote: This is the dataset used in the paper: Detecting Causal Language Use in Science Findings.

training_data.name: MedMCQA
training_data.quote: MedMCQA has more than 194k high-quality AIIMS & NEET PG entrance exam MCQs covering 2.4k healthcare topics and 21 medical subjects.

training_data.name: BigBIO MedQA
training_data.quote: We utilized the English 4-option multiple-choice format (11,290 samples), focusing on clinical reasoning, differential diagnosis, patient management, and medical decision-making across all major medical specialties.

training_data.name: PubMedQA
training_data.quote: The task of PubMedQA is to answer research questions with yes/no/maybe using the corresponding abstracts. PubMedQA has 1k expert-annotated, 61.2k unlabeled and 211.3k artificially generated QA instances.

training_data.name: MedQuAD
training_data.quote: MedQuAD: We used the Medical Question-Answer Dataset compiled from authoritative NIH websites, incorporating 14,553 samples of consumer health questions.

training_data.name: HealthCareMagic
training_data.quote: HealthCareMagic: We incorporated real-world patient-doctor conversation transcripts from healthcare forums (64,246 samples). Data are available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/lee3251/HealthCareMagic.

training_data.name: MIMIC-III
training_data.quote: MIMIC-III | 465,200 | Clinical notes | Clinical | Generative. MIMIC-III is distributed under the PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data License.

training_data.name: UMLS Metathesaurus
training_data.quote: UMLS Metathesaurus | 312,450 | Encyclopedic | Basic science | Open QA. UMLS requires acceptance of the UMLS Metathesaurus License.

training_data.quote: Alpaca-EN-AN: Data are available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/tatsu-lab/alpaca. Alpaca is a dataset of 52,000 instructions and demonstrations generated by OpenAI's text-davinci-003 engine.

training_method.update_scope_quote: QLoRA fine-tuning (4-bit NF4 base + LoRA, r=128, α=256, all linear layers), then merge_and_unload() into the base

source_claims.quote: the LLaMA 3.2 3B model offers a balanced trade-off between computational efficiency and capacity

description.text:
A full, ready-to-use medical model: Llama-3.2-3B adapted to the medical domain with QLoRA, with the LoRA weights merged back into the base. Load it directly with transformers — no adapter, no PEFT, no extra steps. For the lightweight LoRA-adapter version (apply on top of the base yourself), see the link below.

This is the 3B (balanced / mid-tier) member of the Med-LLaMA3 family introduced in the paper “Med-LLaMA3: Advancing Medical Question-Answering Through Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models” (Applied Sciences, 2026). The family adapts the LLaMA-3 architecture to the medical domain by training only a small fraction of the base model’s parameters (5.70% for this 3B variant), achieving strong medical question-answering performance while keeping the memory footprint low — enabling development and inference on low-cost, consumer-grade hardware.

serving.system_prompt: You are a knowledgeable medical assistant. Answer accurately and concisely.
serving.notes: tokenizer_config.json has no chat_template key; the template is the separate chat_template.jinja file, the stock Llama 3.2 template (Cutting Knowledge Date: December 2023). It does not hardcode the medical assistant sentence; that sentence is only in the card's usage example. The card's example uses max_new_tokens=256, do_sample=False, and temperature=0.0. Released weights are bfloat16; the Hub safetensors header reports 3,212,749,824 BF16 parameters. No adapter_config.json is in this repo.

evaluation_reported.text: The card reports 5-shot accuracy on eight MMLU medical subsets for Med-LLaMA3.2-3B: Anatomy 59.52, Clinical Knowledge 68.17, College Biology 71.53, College Medicine 57.65, Medical Genetics 75.00, Nutrition 68.32, Professional Medicine 70.59, Virology 43.17, mean 64.24. The paper's Table 7 prints the same 3B row. The paper's Table 6 (MedMCQA, MedQA, PubMedQA) is reported for the 8B model, not this 3B checkpoint.

discrepancies: Inventory method (qlora) and parent match the card YAML. Inventory datasets match the card YAML list. The card prose and the compiled-dataset card also name MedQuAD, HealthCareMagic, MIMIC-III, UMLS, MedDialog, Alpaca-EN-AN, ChatDoctor (iCliniq), and CovidDialog, which are not in the inventory row. The 3B training script sets num_epochs to 6; the card and paper Table 5 say 5.
